headline: Google has launched Universal Cart, a shared shopping cart that tracks products across Search and the Gemini app, for US users.
score_reason: Confirmed launch by Google of a feature previewed in May; consumer tool with limited reach beyond the US.
importance_line: US shoppers get one cart that follows price drops and restocks across retailers, while retailers and AI shopping agents are tied together through Google's checkout standard, though how widely shops adopt it is not yet clear.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Google said on Thursday that Universal Cart, a tool for collecting and tracking products found in Search and the Gemini app, is now available to US users after a preview at Google I/O in May. It can gather items from several retailers, send alerts when a price drops or an item is back in stock, weigh credit card perks and surface promo codes, and checks out through Google's Universal Commerce Protocol, an open standard meant to let AI agents and retailers work together.
notes: Launch is today; the May preview is background.
